title: Can I BEAT Beyond the Board?
summary: The creator plays the demo of Beyond the Board, a minimalist single-player 3D puzzle adventure. It opens as a winning chess position for White; when he gives check, the board's pieces are 'kidnapped' and the black king flees into the abyss, so he must chase it as a lone rook across floating checkered platforms. After capturing the king on a plank, the rook falls into the abyss ('the sinking hymn') and solves puzzle rooms: buttons with tick counters that move platforms or raise columns for N turns ('Switches speak in sequence'), wall symbols with hints, a moat crossing, and finally the Eldritch King boss which gains hexagons each turn and fires a beam on its 4th hexagon - he hides behind enemy rooks so the beam eliminates them, then presses buttons that elevate the king so the rook can capture it. The demo ends after that.
rules: Player controls a single white rook (moves like a rook, turn-based) on floating 3D checkered platforms; hold left button to keep moving; right button rotates camera.
Buttons: stepping/clicking a button starts a tick counter (number shown over the rook); the linked platform/column moves into place and returns when the counter runs out.
Enemy rooks capture you if you step into their line of sight; death respawns you on the same level.

Eldritch King boss: gains a hexagon each turn and fires a beam along its line when it reaches 4 hexagons (fires before enemy rooks move); standing behind an enemy rook makes the beam destroy that rook; enemy rooks cycle middle/corner positions.
Final phase: the king fires every turn; buttons elevate the king onto a platform so the rook can look up the tower and capture it.
Hints are revealed by clicking wall symbols.
win_condition: Capture the Eldritch King at the end of the demo (puzzle progression).
